title: Define safety contracts and runtime checks for KV cache reclamation across LRU/TTL/prefix-aware policies
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: As continuous batching and high-concurrency inference grow, the KV cache on GPUs must reclaim memory safely across different policy modes (LRU, TTL, and prefix-aware). We need precise runtime contracts that guarantee correctness (no silent corruption or prefix bleed), predictable GC behavior under pressure, and measurable SLO impact. This ticket scopes formal safety contracts, runtime checks, and a test harness to exercise corner cases across policies and mixed workloads.

Goals:
- Define minimal correctness invariants for cache reclamation across LRU/TTL/prefix scopes (atomicity, prefix isolation, staleness bounds).
- Specify runtime checks and assertion points that can run in opt-in debug builds and in production with low overhead (sampling).
- Design contract tests and deterministic replay harnesses that exercise eviction under high-batch, prefetch, and migration events.
- Produce migration plan and canary rollout for runtime-2.4 that includes telemetry and automatic rollback criteria.

Out of scope: full rework of cache architecture or new allocation algorithm designs (separate RFC ticket).
acceptance_criteria: 1) A short formal document (<=6 pages) listing invariants for each policy and their interactions exists in Confluence; 2) Runtime assertions implemented behind flags with <1% p99 latency regression when disabled and <5% sampling cost when enabled; 3) Contract test suite (deterministic replay + randomized fuzz) runs in CI and bucketed nightly; 4) Canary run plan, dashboards and rollback thresholds are approved by SRE and PM; 5) Security review completed for assertion telemetry and KMS-tagged audit logs.
design_notes:
We propose three primitives: Pin(token) to mark a prefix as non-evictable for request lifetime, Lease(epoch) to coordinate cross-worker reclamation, and SoftTTL that permits reclamation after a grace period but keeps pointer staleness bounds for callers. Key decisions: prefer per-prefix soft eviction windows (ms scale) vs global compaction intervals; adopt strong isolation for 'critical' prefixes (customer-owned metadata) via explicit pinning; avoid synchronous cross-GPU invalidation—use epoch-based fencing and background scavenger.

Trade-offs: Per-prefix locks increase metadata overhead but reduce incorrect cross-tenant prefix leakage. Sampling runtime assertions reduces overhead but may miss rare races. Epoch fencing increases reclamation latency under pressure but simplifies correctness proofs.
implementation_steps: 1) Write invariants doc and circulate (owner: Miguel). 2) Add debug-mode assertions and a low-overhead sampled assertion path (owner: eng-kv). 3) Implement Pin and Lease lightweight APIs in runtime core (owner: runtime-team). 4) Build deterministic replay harness using production trace snippets (owner: infra-testing). 5) Add CI contract tests + nightly fuzzers (owner: qa). 6) Create canary dashboard with mem pressure and correctness signals (owner: observability). 7) Run internal canary on Dedicated cluster + roll to hosted with feature flag and rollback policy (owner: releases).
progress_updates: 2025-11-04 - Created ticket. Initial scoping and list of goals. Assigned to Miguel.
2025-11-18 - Draft invariants doc uploaded to Confluence: link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/KV+Reclamation+Safety (internal). Requested review from SRE and Security.

2025-12-02 - Spike complete: implemented epoch fencing prototype in a private branch (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8196). Early microbenchmarks show ~0.4% p50 overhead when disabled, 1.8% when sampling at 5%.
2025-12-11 - Design review with SRE and PM. Action: move hard TTL into softTTL+grace to avoid thundering reclamation under bursty workloads. Added explicit Pin API for per-request prefix safety.

2026-01-03 - CI contract harness scaffold merged (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/qa/pull/224). Deterministic replayer can replay batched eviction sequence from trace id sample-20251218-7. Fuzzer seeds added.
2026-01-12 - Security review kickoff. Discussed telemetry anonymization and KMS tagging for assertion dumps. Plan to ship assertions behind feature flag and sampling mode for hosted customers.
review_feedback: SRE (Jordan Lee) - Approved invariants but requested explicit metric for 'prefix-staleness' and an alert if >1% of requests hit stale entries within 10s of reclamation.
Security (Priya Nair) - Require telemetry payload scrubbing and KMS encryption of any captured keys. Also requested retention policy for assertion dumps (30 days max).
PM (Ethan Cho) - Wants clear customer-facing notes for Dedicated customers about possible increased mem pressure during canary and rollback steps.
risks: 1) Assertion telemetry may capture sensitive keys if not scrubbed; mitigated by KMS and redaction. 2) Sampling can miss rare races — randomized fuzz and CI nightly runs mitigate. 3) Pin abuse could starve reclamation for long-running prefixes — enforce TTL on pins and token expiry.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for invariants and fence transitions.
- Integration tests: deterministic replay of production traces with induced GC pressure.
- Fuzz tests: randomized sequence of Pin/Lease/Put/Delete under multi-worker concurrency.
- Performance tests: microbenchmarks to measure assertion overhead and memory reclamation latency under mixed workloads.
- Canary: run on 5% of Dedicated nodes for 2 weeks with rollback on >0.5% customer errors or >10% mem pressure spike.
next_steps: Finalize invariants doc after security feedback (Miguel). Complete debug assertions and sampling path (eng-kv by 2026-01-20). Merge CI contract tests and enable nightly fuzzing. Schedule SRE canary and dashboard by 2026-01-30.
notes_for_release: Feature gated behind 'kv_reclaim_safety' flag. Default: disabled for hosted; enabled in debug images. For Dedicated customers, coordinate with account team before enabling. Rollout plan and rollback criteria in release runbook.
estimated_impact: Expected improvement in correctness assurance and reduction in rare user-facing stale-cache incidents. Short-term cost: added CI time and minor runtime overhead when sampling assertions. Long-term: fewer incidents and more predictable mem usage under mixed policy workloads.
